pages.text: Kota and a young hippo raced across the yard. Tumble! Kota tripped over a stone. "Waaah!" Their cries filled the yard.
Only a little dirt marked Kota's knee. Still, Kota sat and sobbed. The hippo shuffled helplessly beside them.
"Does it hurt a lot?" the hippo asked. "...I don't know. The tears just come." Kota sniffled on the ground.
Dad came and checked their knee. "No bleeding. You got a fright. Shall I teach you Brush, Brush, Up You Jump?" Kota looked up, sniffling.
"First, say 'Ouch!' nice and loud." "Ouuuch!" Kota called. Their chest felt a little clearer. "Good. Now brush, brush!"
Kota brushed the dirt off their knee. As it fell away, the tears stopped, too. "Oh! It doesn't hurt at all now."
"Last, up you jump!" Kota sprang up and landed on both feet. The hippo clapped. Kota's tail shot skyward.
They raced again. The hippo tumbled—then jumped right up. "Ouch, brush, brush, up you jump!" They laughed together.
Now, when Kota fell, they brushed their knee and counted. "One, ouch! Two, brush, brush! Three, up you jump!" Up came Kota before the tears.
That evening, Dad blew gently on Kota's knee and hugged them. "A fall can teach us how to get up." "Next time, brush, brush, up you jump!" Kota hopped to show him.
